dedupe_keys.name: opensees open system for earthquake engineering simulation

description: OpenSees is a software framework for building applications that simulate how structural and geotechnical systems perform in earthquakes, developed as open source under sponsorship of the Pacific Earthquake Engineering Research Center to improve modelling and computation in earthquake engineering. Several applications are released on its site, with interpreters in Tcl and Python to which users can add elements and materials; version 3.8.0 of the binary was released in February 2026 after 3.7.1 in January 2025, and the site points to NHERI SimCenter tools built on OpenSees and to material on uncertainty quantification. Coverage: generic, any structure or soil system. Access: free download of binaries and source, a wiki and a message board; registration is encouraged. Licence: University of California terms allowing free non-commercial use by educational, research and non-profit bodies and internal use by others. Caveats: the developers warn that it changes often, and commercial redistribution needs separate permission. Simulation uses: nonlinear response histories that feed building fragility, loss and regional resilience models. Related records: pelicun, the SimCenter R2D tool and the FEMA P-58 PACT tool.
